cues.en: I make videos about how walkable cities are more efficient, more environmentally friendly, more financially sustainable, and just better places to live.
cues.zh: 我制作视频，探讨适宜步行的城市如何更高效、更环保、财政上更可持续，以及更适宜居住。

cues.en: So given these benefits, it's not surprising that cities all around the world are trying to build more mixed use walkable neighborhoods and viable alternatives to driving.
cues.zh: 鉴于这些好处，世界各地的城市都在努力建设更多功能混合的步行社区，并提供可行的驾车替代方案，这并不奇怪。

cues.en: Unfortunately,
cues.zh: 不幸的是，

cues.en: as engineers, planners and advocates try to repair the mistakes of the nineteen sixties and build the cities of the future, there's a growing trend that could undo all of that hard work.
cues.zh: 正当工程师、规划师和倡导者试图弥补 20 世纪 60 年代的错误、建设未来之城时，一股日益抬头的趋势可能会毁掉这一切努力。

cues.en: The growth of SUVs and light trucks.
cues.zh: 那就是 SUV 和轻型卡车的激增。

cues.en: I really don't think it's an exaggeration to say that if there's a positive goal that cities have for the future, SUVs fight against that. They're just bad for cities.
cues.zh: 毫不夸张地说，只要是城市对未来的积极愿景，SUV 都在与之背道而驰。它们对城市百害而无一利。

cues.en: Really bad.
cues.zh: 真的非常糟糕。

cues.en: If you're walking and you get hit by an SUV, you're three times more likely to die than if you've been hit by a regular car. And if you're in that regular car, you're more likely to die in a crash if it's with an SUV.
cues.zh: 如果你走路时被一辆 SUV 撞到，致死率是普通轿车的 3 倍。而如果你坐在普通轿车里，与 SUV 相撞的致死率也更高。

cues.en: SUVs are more likely to hit people in the first place because they're big, unwieldy, and have poor visibility.
cues.zh: 而且 SUV 本身就更容易撞到人，因为它们体型庞大、笨重，而且视野很差。

cues.en: SUV drivers themselves are twice as likely to be killed in a rollover than car drivers.
cues.zh: 至于 SUV 驾驶员自己，在翻车事故中的死亡概率也是普通轿车司机的两倍。

cues.en: SUVs make congestion worse because they take up more space on the roads, they have terrible fuel economy too, and the list goes on and on.
cues.zh: SUV 还会加剧拥堵，因为它们占用更多道路空间，油耗也很糟糕，缺点简直数不胜数。

cues.en: And to be completely honest, I'm making this video because I'm absolutely fed up with the conversation around SUVs and light trucks. We're constantly being told that doing anything about the astronomical
cues.zh: 说实话，我做这个视频是因为我实在受够了围绕 SUV 和轻卡的说辞。总有人对我们说，要是限制这种惊人的

cues.en: growth and the average size of motor vehicles would infringe on the freedoms of people to do whatever they want.
cues.zh: 激增以及机动车平均尺寸的膨胀，就会侵犯人们随心所欲的自由。

cues.en: But your freedom to swing your arm ends where my face begins, and SUVs are a giant punch in the face to everyone who doesn't drive one.
cues.zh: 但你挥舞手臂的自由止于我的鼻尖，而 SUV 就像是狠狠打在每一个不开 SUV 的人脸上的一记重拳。

cues.en: In short, SUVs are oversized, ridiculous, unnecessary death machines that are literally killing people, even their own drivers. So let's look at why they're so popular.
cues.zh: 简而言之，SUV 是一种臃肿、荒谬、多余的杀人机器，真的在夺走人命，甚至包括驾驶员自己。那么，我们来看看它们为何如此流行。

cues.en: If you went back in time about forty years, you wouldn't really see any SUVs.
cues.zh: 如果你回到大约 40 年前，街上几乎看不到什么 SUV。

cues.en: If you lived in a rural area, you might see a small pickup truck or a bare bones Jeep used for hunting or farming.
cues.zh: 如果你住在农村，可能会看到用来打猎或务农的小皮卡或简配 Jeep。

cues.en: But until fairly recently,
cues.zh: 但直到不久前，

cues.en: pretty much everybody drove a car or maybe a van.
cues.zh: 几乎所有人开的还是轿车，或者小客车。

cues.en: But today, light trucks and SUVs make up almost 80%
cues.zh: 可如今，轻卡和 SUV 几乎占了

cues.en: of all new car sales in The US. 80%.
cues.zh: 全美所有新车销量的 80%。整整 80%。

cues.en: The auto industry has been heavily pushing these vehicles for years and it's been done to avoid regulations,
cues.zh: 多年来，汽车行业一直在大力推广这类车型，以此来钻监管的空子，

cues.en: meaning more profit for car manufacturers.
cues.zh: 这意味着车企能赚取更多利润。

cues.en: This is possible because in America SUVs are classified as light trucks, which aren't subject to the same safety and emission standards as cars.
cues.zh: 之所以能这样，是因为在美国 SUV 被划归为轻型卡车，不必遵守与轿车同等严格的安全和排放标准。

cues.en: Light trucks originally referred to commercial vehicles that needed to carry or tow heavy loads or traverse difficult terrain.
cues.zh: 轻型卡车最初指需要运载或拖拽重物、或穿越复杂地形的商用车辆。

cues.en: To facilitate this, light trucks have large engines and stiff frames, both of which are disastrous for fuel economy and safety, but more on that in a second.
cues.zh: 为了做到这一点，轻卡配备大发动机和刚性车架，这对燃油经济性和安全性都很不利，不过这点稍后再讲。

cues.en: And it all started because of these chickens.
cues.zh: 而这一切都始于这些鸡。

cues.en: Europe placed a heavy import tax on American chickens. In retaliation,
cues.zh: 欧洲对美国鸡肉征收高额进口税。作为报复，

cues.en: America levied import taxes of their own.
cues.zh: 美国也征收了自己的进口税。

cues.en: They specifically targeted European light trucks that were typically used by small businesses.
cues.zh: 他们专门针对欧洲轻卡，这类车通常由小企业使用。

cues.en: And since foreign automakers were already producing better and cheaper cars,
cues.zh: 而且由于外国车企已经在生产更好、更便宜的汽车，

cues.en: the declining American auto industry really wanted to shift to a vehicle where they didn't have to compete because like competition is for suckers.
cues.zh: 日渐衰落的美国汽车业非常想转向一种不必竞争的车型，因为竞争嘛，是给傻子准备的。

cues.en: So that carved out light trucks as its own category in America. But what really kicked off the explosion of SUVs was ironically
cues.zh: 这让轻卡在美国被划成了一个独立类别。但真正引爆SUV热潮的，讽刺的是

cues.en: fuel efficiency regulations.
cues.zh: 燃油效率法规。

cues.en: The corporate average fuel economy or CAFE standards required all automobile manufacturers in The US to improve the average fuel economy of their entire fleet or face financial penalties.
cues.zh: 企业平均燃油经济性（CAFE）标准要求美国所有汽车制造商提高其整个车队的平均燃油经济性，否则将面临罚款。

cues.en: But here's the catch.
cues.zh: 但问题在于。

cues.en: American automakers lobbied hard so that light trucks were classified differently than passenger cars.
cues.zh: 美国车企大力游说，使轻卡被归类为与乘用车不同的类别。

cues.en: This was necessary,
cues.zh: 他们辩称，这是必要的，

cues.en: they argued, because unlike cars, light trucks were used by honest, hardworking, red blooded American patriots. So rather than build cars that met cafe standards, auto manufacturers were incentivized to get as many people to buy light trucks as possible.
cues.zh: 因为与轿车不同，轻卡是诚实、勤劳、热血的美国爱国者使用的。于是，汽车制造商不是去造符合CAFE标准的轿车，而是被激励尽可能让更多人购买轻卡。

cues.en: The first SUVs could classified as light trucks because they were built in the same factories and using the same body on frame construction as traditional pickup trucks.
cues.zh: 最早的SUV能归类为轻卡，因为它们与传统皮卡在同样的工厂生产，并使用相同的非承载式车身结构。

cues.en: These SUVs were basically pickup trucks with a longer roof.
cues.zh: 这些SUV基本上就是车顶更长的皮卡。

cues.en: This allowed American car manufacturers to save a lot of money by using existing design parts and factories. And, of course, it also allowed them to avoid any regulations for passenger vehicles, including safety regulations because these were, after all, light trucks.
cues.zh: 这使美国汽车制造商能利用现有设计零件和工厂省下大量资金。当然，这也让他们避开了所有乘用车法规，包括安全法规，因为毕竟这些是轻卡。

cues.en: So this saved the auto manufacturers a lot of money and avoided regulations.
cues.zh: 所以这为汽车制造商省了很多钱，也避开了法规。

cues.en: But there was a problem.
cues.zh: 但有一个问题。

cues.en: How were they going to convince people to buy a vehicle that was impractical,
cues.zh: 他们要怎么说服人们购买一种不实用、

cues.en: uncomfortable, ugly, and dangerous?
cues.zh: 不舒服、丑陋又危险的汽车？

cues.en: The book High and Mighty, written by a Detroit automobile journalist and published in 2002,
cues.zh: 《High and Mighty》一书由底特律一位汽车记者撰写，于2002年出版，

cues.en: documents the history of how SUVs came to be. And it was one of the books that helped radicalize me against car dependency.
cues.zh: 记录了SUV如何兴起的历史。它也是促使我彻底反对汽车依赖的书籍之一。

cues.en: And while this book is rather out of date today, the history of the SUV is still very relevant.
cues.zh: 虽然这本书如今已经相当过时，但SUV的历史仍然很有现实意义。

cues.en: The earliest SUVs were Jeeps marketed to rich guys who went hunting on the weekends. Marketers used this outdoorsy image to lure people who wanted to be cool.
cues.zh: 最早的 SUV 是卖给周末去打猎的有钱人的 Jeep。营销人员利用这种户外形象来吸引那些想要变酷的人。

cues.en: Hey, you might live in suburbia and work a super lame desk job in a business park, but you're still the kind of guy who might maybe someday go on a camping trip and this is the car to do it in. No. No. Don't look at that significantly more practical car over there. Station wagons are for losers and boomers.
cues.zh: 嘿，你可能住在郊区，在写字楼里干着超无聊的坐班工作，但你骨子里依然是个说不定哪天就会去露营的人，而这辆车正是为此而生。别，千万别看旁边那辆实用得多的车，旅行车那是给窝囊废和老古董开的。

cues.en: And this marketing approach saw some modest success, but the real winning strategy was to make scared people feel safe.
cues.zh: 这种营销手段取得了一定的成效，但真正制胜的策略，是让内心害怕的人感到安全。

cues.en: Early focus groups showed that Americans were obsessed with crime and violence, so automobile manufacturers took advantage of that.
cues.zh: 早期的焦点小组调研显示，美国人对犯罪和暴力极度焦虑，汽车制造商便趁机利用了这一点。

cues.en: The city is a big scary place. Protect yourself with a big stupid car.
cues.zh: 城市是个危险可怕的地方，用一辆傻大的车来保护自己吧。

cues.en: That's how we got ads that say think of it as 4,000 pound guardian angel.
cues.zh: 于是就有了这样的广告：“把它当成你重达 4000 磅的守护天使”。

cues.en: And this one that says let nature worry about you for a change which addresses the incredibly common suburbanite problem of crocodiles attacking you from trees.
cues.zh: 还有这句“换大自然来为你担惊受怕吧”，完美解决了郊区居民极常遇到的——鳄鱼从树上扑下来袭击人的问题。

cues.en: This also turned road safety into an arms race. Whoever has the biggest vehicle wins, and so vehicles became bigger and more aggressive every year.
cues.zh: 这也把道路安全变成了一场军备竞赛。谁的车最大谁就赢，于是车辆一年比一年更大、更具攻击性。

cues.en: It's got to the point where you can't even buy a small practical fuel efficient car in America anymore even if you wanted to.
cues.zh: 事态已经发展到就算你想买，在美国也根本买不到小巧、实用且省油的车了。

cues.en: When we lived in Brussels, for example, we owned a Toyota Aigo, which was perfect for our family. But Toyota doesn't even sell this model in America. I
cues.zh: 比如我们住在布鲁塞尔时开的是一辆 Toyota Aigo，对我们家来说再完美不过了。但 Toyota 根本不在美国卖这款车。我

cues.en: wonder why.
cues.zh: 很好奇这是为什么。

cues.en: So where does it all end? When everyone is driving tanks?
cues.zh: 那这一切什么时候才是个头？等到所有人都开坦克吗？

cues.en: Tanks. What a funny joke. Right?
cues.zh: 坦克，真是个好笑的笑话，对吧？

cues.en: Except that this is one of the largest Sherman tanks from World War two.
cues.zh: 只不过，眼前这是一辆二战时期尺寸最大的 Sherman 坦克。

cues.en: And this is a Cadillac Escalade.
cues.zh: 而这是一辆 Cadillac Escalade。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: Incidentally, the website where I got these images of cars, SUVs, and trucks, but not tanks, is carsize.com,
cues.zh: 顺便提一句，我找到这些轿车、SUV 和皮卡（但不包括坦克）图片的网站是 carsize.com，

cues.en: an excellent and addictive site that lets you easily compare the sizes of many different kinds of vehicles. They were also nice enough to let me use their vehicle photos in this video, so check them out. I put a link in the description, but like, just type in carsized.com
cues.zh: 一个非常棒且让人上头的网站，能让你轻松对比各种车型的尺寸。他们还非常好心地允许我在视频中使用这些车辆图片，大家可以去看看。我在简介里放了链接，不过其实直接输入 carsized.com 就行，

cues.en: yourself. It's really not that hard.
cues.zh: 这真的没那么难。

cues.en: It's incredibly depressing that SUVs were marketed as being safer because their classification as light trucks has been disastrous for actual safety.
cues.zh: 令人极度沮丧的是，SUV 竟然被宣传得更安全，而实际上把它归类为轻型卡车对真正的安全而言是一场灾难。

cues.en: One of the most dangerous things about SUVs is their bumper height. American cars are required to have bumpers between 16 to 20 inches off the ground. But surprise, light trucks don't have to deal with that regulation, so they can have their bumpers pretty much as high as they want.
cues.zh: SUV 最危险的一点就是保险杠高度。美国轿车被强制要求保险杠离地高度在 16 到 20 英寸之间。但意不意外，轻型卡车不受这项法规约束，所以它们的保险杠基本想造多高就造多高。

cues.en: SUVs were also stiffer than cars. The original light trucks were built to haul or tow heavy weights, which means they needed a heavier, stiffer chassis.
cues.zh: SUV 的车身刚度也比普通轿车更硬。最初的轻型卡车是为了运载或拖曳重物而造的，这意味着它们需要更重、更坚硬的底盘。

cues.en: Rather than crumpling in a crash like a car frame, which distributes energy and acts as a protective cushion, the chassis on a light truck acted like a battering ram, and the people inside became the crumple zone.
cues.zh: 轻型卡车的底盘不像轿车车架那样在碰撞中溃缩、分散能量并充当保护缓冲垫，而是像攻城锤一样撞上去，车里的人反倒成了溃缩区。

cues.en: Combine that with a high bumper, and you run into a problem known as crash compatibility.
cues.zh: 再配上高保险杠，就会遇到所谓的碰撞兼容性问题。

cues.en: When two normal sized cars crash into each other, they are compatible and that their safety features are pretty much aligned and designed to work together, which provides more protection to the drivers of both cars.
cues.zh: 两辆普通尺寸的汽车相撞时，它们是兼容的，安全配置基本对齐，设计上能协同工作，从而给两车驾驶员提供更多保护。

cues.en: But when a regular car and an SUV crash into each other, the bigger, higher, stiffer vehicle doesn't line up with the smaller car's safety features, which can make the crash more deadly.
cues.zh: 但当普通轿车和 SUV 相撞时，更大、更高、更硬的车辆无法与较小车辆的安全配置对齐，这会让碰撞更致命。

cues.en: Of course, it's even worse for anyone outside of a car.
cues.zh: 当然，对车外的人来说更糟。

cues.en: When a person gets hit by a car, they're typically thrown onto the hood. This can cause injury to the lower legs which sucks but generally doesn't kill you at low speeds.
cues.zh: 人被汽车撞到时，通常会被抛到引擎盖上。这会伤到小腿，虽然很糟，但低速下一般不会致命。

cues.en: But the higher front end of an SUV means the impact is centered near the torso and head which is much more deadly.
cues.zh: 但 SUV 更高的车头意味着撞击会集中在躯干和头部附近，这要致命得多。

cues.en: People hit by SUVs are also more likely to hit their head on the ground or go under the vehicle thanks to their high ground clearance. And in case it isn't obvious,
cues.zh: 被 SUV 撞到的人还更容易头部撞地，或因为离地间隙高而被卷入车底。万一这还不明显，

cues.en: it's a bad thing to be underneath a gigantic heavy light truck.
cues.zh: 被压在一辆又大又重的轻型卡车下面，可不是什么好事。

cues.en: And what makes this all even more insane is that most of the features that make SUV drivers feel safe actually make them
cues.zh: 更离谱的是，让 SUV 司机感觉安全的大多数配置，实际上反而让他们

cues.en: more dangerous.
cues.zh: 更危险。

cues.en: Many buyers say they wanted an SUV because you sit up high while driving them which gives better visibility, but that's not really true. It might make it easier to see farther down the road, but it's actually harder to see stuff right in front of you.
cues.zh: 许多买家说想买 SUV，是因为坐得高、视野更好，但事实并非如此。坐得高也许更容易看清远处路面，但看清正前方的东西其实更难。

cues.en: The advocacy group Kids and Cars put 17 children in front of an SUV and they couldn't see any of them from the driver's seat.
cues.zh: 倡导组织 Kids and Cars 把 17 个孩子放在一辆 SUV 前方，结果从驾驶座一个都看不到。

cues.en: Since the introduction of SUVs, there has been a massive increase in what are called frontovers.
cues.zh: 自从 SUV 普及以来，所谓“前部盲区碾压”事故大幅增加。

cues.en: A person, usually a child, getting run over by an SUV by a driver who can't even see them.
cues.zh: 一个人，通常是孩子，被根本看不见他的 SUV 司机碾过。

cues.en: Kids and cars have been documenting the rise of frontovers in America and the results are shocking.
cues.zh: Kids and Cars 一直在记录美国前部盲区碾压事故的上升情况，结果令人震惊。

cues.en: But before we move on, I want you to look at this chart and understand what you're seeing.
cues.zh: 但在继续之前，我想让你看看这张图，弄明白你在看什么。

cues.en: This is saying that over a ten year period, over five hundred American children were killed by being run over by SUVs,
cues.zh: 这张图说明，在十年间，有超过五百名美国儿童被 SUV 碾死，

cues.en: usually by their own parents in their own driveways.
cues.zh: 而且通常是在自家车道上，被自己的父母碾死。

cues.en: This is insane.
cues.zh: 这太离谱了。

cues.en: This is legitimately
cues.zh: 这真的

cues.en: insane.
cues.zh: 太离谱了。

cues.en: In any civilized society, this information alone would be enough to regulate the hood design of SUVs and light trucks.
cues.zh: 在任何文明社会，仅凭这些信息就足以监管 SUV 和轻型卡车的引擎盖设计。

cues.en: But instead, the industry solution
cues.zh: 但相反，行业的解决方案

cues.en: for this is proximity sensors and front facing cameras because car companies are happy for any regulations that means they can sell you more stuff.
cues.zh: 却是接近传感器和前置摄像头，因为车企乐意接受任何能让他们多卖东西的监管规定。

cues.en: Now, I personally believe that drivers should be looking at the road and not a screen inside their SUV. But hey, what do I know? I'm just a weirdo who objects to children being run over by trucks.
cues.zh: 我个人认为，司机应该看路，而不是看SUV里的屏幕。但嘿，我懂什么呀？我只是个反对孩子被卡车碾过的怪人。

cues.en: If you agree with me, then you can sign the consumer reports petition link in the description.
cues.zh: 如果你同意我，可以点简介里的 Consumer Reports 请愿链接签名。

cues.en: Light trucks are usually four wheel drive as well, which is pitched as another safety feature.
cues.zh: 轻型卡车通常也配四驱，这被宣传成又一项安全特性。

cues.en: Four wheel drive is great for accelerating in slippery conditions like mud, but what four wheel drive doesn't do is help you slow down.
cues.zh: 四驱很擅长在泥地这种湿滑条件下加速，但四驱做不到的是帮你减速。

cues.en: That means overconfident SUV drivers can go as fast as they want in bad conditions
cues.zh: 这意味着过度自信的SUV司机在恶劣条件下想开多快就开多快

cues.en: as long as they're not planning on stopping.
cues.zh: 只要他们不打算停车。

cues.en: Maybe that's fine in a rural setting, but these land yachts are all over American cities.
cues.zh: 也许在农村还行，但这些陆地游艇遍布美国城市。

cues.en: I once drove across Texas in the middle of a once in a decade snowstorm and there was literally a light truck in the ditch every few miles while my rear wheel drive Oldsmobile pushed through without any issues.
cues.zh: 我有一次在十年一遇的暴风雪中横穿得州，每隔几英里就真有一辆轻型卡车陷在沟里，而我的后驱 Oldsmobile 一路开过去毫无问题。

cues.en: Though part of this is because SUV owners are more likely to be bad drivers. That's not just my opinion. Car companies paid millions of dollars for market research to find this out.
cues.zh: 不过部分原因是SUV车主更可能是糟糕的司机。这不只是我的看法。车企花了几百万美元做市场调研才发现这一点。

cues.en: People who gravitate toward SUVs tend to be less confident in their driving abilities and rely on the large size of the vehicle to keep them quote unquote
cues.zh: 倾向于选择SUV的人往往对自己的驾驶能力不太自信，并依赖车辆的大尺寸来让自己所谓的

cues.en: safe at the expense of everyone else.
cues.zh: 安全，代价是其他所有人。

cues.en: What made this even worse is that in the early days, most SUV buyers were assholes.
cues.zh: 更糟的是，早期大多数SUV买家都是混蛋。

cues.en: I'm not being flippant in suggesting that all SUV drivers were assholes, but assholes were literally the primary target market when automakers wanted to make SUVs mainstream.
cues.zh: 我不是在轻率地说所有SUV司机都是混蛋，但车企想让SUV成为主流时，混蛋就是字面意义上的主要目标市场。

cues.en: Auto industry research determined that the average light truck purchaser was obsessed with status,
cues.zh: 汽车行业研究发现，普通轻型卡车购买者痴迷于地位，

cues.en: less likely to volunteer or feel a strong connection to their communities,
cues.zh: 更不可能做志愿者，也不太会对自己的社区有强烈归属感，

cues.en: less giving, less oriented toward others,
cues.zh: 更不慷慨，更少考虑他人，

cues.en: more afraid of crime, more likely to text and drive, more likely to take risks while driving, and more likely to think stuff like this looks cool. What thought?
cues.zh: 更害怕犯罪，更可能边发短信边开车，更可能开车冒险，也更可能觉得这种东西看起来很酷。什么想法？

cues.en: Ten years ago, a baby faced Mark Rober put plastic animals on the side of the road to see which ones were most likely to get hit.
cues.zh: 十年前，娃娃脸的 Mark Rober 把塑料动物放在路边，看哪些最容易被撞。

cues.en: He found that some drivers would purposefully swerve to run over the animals.
cues.zh: 他发现有些司机故意打方向去碾这些动物。

cues.en: And eighty nine percent of those people who tried to murder animals were driving SUVs.
cues.zh: 而那些试图谋杀动物的人里，89%开的是SUV。

cues.en: Yep. The market research is correct. These people are assholes.
cues.zh: 没错。市场调研是对的。这些人就是混蛋。

cues.en: But you know what SUV drivers are typically not?
cues.zh: 但你知道SUV司机通常不是什么吗？

cues.en: Outdoorsy.
cues.zh: 爱户外。

cues.en: SUVs are marketed for going off road, towing a boat, or for going camping. But in reality,
cues.zh: SUV被营销成能越野、拖船或露营。但现实中，

cues.en: of light truck owners tow something once a year or less, and 70% go off road once a year or less. In fact, the vast majority of SUVs are driven in cities and will never go off road. They are just used for everyday tasks like commuting and buying groceries.
cues.zh: 的轻型卡车车主每年拖东西不超过一次，70%每年越野不超过一次。事实上，绝大多数SUV都在城市里开，永远不会越野。它们只用于通勤、买菜之类的日常任务。

cues.en: Well, I guess they go off road when the driver is texting and plows into a building or something.
cues.zh: 好吧，我猜他们所谓的“越野”，大概是指司机边发短信边一头撞进大楼之类的时候吧。

cues.en: The most outdoorsy people I've met, those who regularly go hiking or camping, drive something like a Subaru Outback Wagon because they're actual adventurous people, not just a bunch of posers and SUVs.
cues.zh: 我见过最喜欢户外的人——那些经常徒步或露营的人——开的反而是 Subaru Outback 旅行车之类的车，因为他们是真正的探险爱好者，而不是开着 SUV 摆造型的装模作样之徒。

cues.en: And Americans seem to think you need some giant truck to tow anything, but you see all kinds of regular cars with trailers in Europe.
cues.zh: 美国人似乎觉得拖任何东西都需要一辆巨型皮卡，但在欧洲，随处可见挂着拖车的普通轿车。

cues.en: And the Dutch in particular are famous for vacationing with their caravans pulled by normal cars.
cues.zh: 尤其是荷兰人，出了名地喜欢用普通轿车拖着房车去度假。

cues.en: Though this recent example was extreme even by Dutch standards.
cues.zh: 不过最近这个例子，哪怕按荷兰人的标准来看也太夸张了。

cues.en: And the reactions to this video will be extremely predictable. People will inevitably claim that these SUVs and pickup drivers need that space for all the stuff they're hauling.
cues.zh: 这个视频的评论区我闭着眼睛都能猜到：肯定会有人辩解说，这些 SUV 和皮卡司机需要那么大的空间来拉货。

cues.en: That somehow SUVs and pickup trucks went from niche rural vehicles
cues.zh: 就好像 SUV 和皮卡从农村的小众车型，

cues.en: to literally the most popular vehicles on the road because of some magical
cues.zh: 变成了马路上最流行的车型，纯粹是因为某种神奇的

cues.en: demographic shift. And if you do live in a rural area, you might need to drive a light truck. And obviously, that's fine and I don't care. But we're talking about suburbia here and come on. You know as well as I do that the vast, vast, vast majority of drivers in these light trucks are carrying exactly two things. Their briefcase and their fat ass. And most people don't use a briefcase anymore.
cues.zh: 人口结构转变。如果你确实住在农村，可能确实需要开轻型卡车，这显然没问题，我完全不在乎。但我们这里聊的是郊区，拜托，你我心知肚明，开这些轻卡的人，绝大绝大绝大多数车里只装了两样东西：公文包和他们肥硕的屁股。而且现在大部分人连公文包都不带了。

cues.en: This is particularly true with so called luxury SUVs.
cues.zh: 尤其是那些所谓的豪华 SUV，更是如此。

cues.en: We all know these aren't hauling shit. Right?
cues.zh: 大家心里都清楚，这些车屁都没拉过，对吧？

cues.en: And the Mercedes g wagon has to be the absolute dumbest luxury vehicle ever made.
cues.zh: 而 Mercedes G-Wagon 绝对是有史以来最愚蠢的豪华车型。

cues.en: I can just imagine the conference room at Mercedes when these were designed. How ugly, uncomfortable and inefficient can we make this thing and still have these rich Voltrottle buy it? We
cues.zh: 我完全能想象当年 Mercedes 设计这玩意儿时的会议室现场：“我们要把这东西造得多丑、多不舒服、多费油，那帮有钱的大蠢蛋才会乖乖掏钱买单？”我们

cues.en: can't just ignore this and say it's personal
cues.zh: 不能对这种现象视而不见，说这只是个人

cues.en: choice because SUVs are a huge problem for cities.
cues.zh: 选择，因为 SUV 对城市来说是个巨大的麻烦。

cues.en: Oversized SUVs take up more space and make congestion worse.
cues.zh: 体型过大的 SUV 占用更多空间，让拥堵雪上加霜。

cues.en: Longer vehicles mean fewer cars get through a light, which means more people gunning it to get through a yellow or red and subsequently slamming into more people trying to cross the street.
cues.zh: 车身更长意味着每个绿灯能通过的车更少，这就导致更多人猛踩油门抢黄灯甚至闯红灯，进而撞倒更多正在过马路的行人。

cues.en: And parking, which is already disastrous in cities, is even worse because of SUVs,
cues.zh: 在城市里停车本来就是场灾难，而 SUV 让情况变得更加恶化，

cues.en: which take up more space at the curb.
cues.zh: 因为它们在路边占用了更大的空间。

cues.en: London, that's real London, is having problems with street parking because SUVs are getting longer so fewer parked vehicles can fit on a street.
cues.zh: 伦敦——我是说真正的英国伦敦——正在为街边停车发愁，因为 SUV 越来越长，一条街上能停下的车就越来越少。

cues.en: Hell, even in fake London these stupid things don't even fit in the giant parking spaces.
cues.zh: 见鬼，哪怕是在“假伦敦”（加拿大伦敦），这帮蠢玩意儿连那里的巨型停车位都停不进去。

cues.en: So new parking spots in new developments are being made bigger, which means bigger parking lots and even more paved surfaces in our cities.
cues.zh: 因此，新建开发区的车位越做越大，这意味着更大的停车场，以及我们城市中更多被水泥硬化的地面。

cues.en: And you'll often find light trucks parked in driveways because they don't fit in a typical garage.
cues.zh: 你经常会看到轻型卡车停在私家车道上，因为一般的车库根本停不下。

cues.en: SUVs are wider too.
cues.zh: SUV 也更宽。

cues.en: Look at how much less space a cyclist has in a world full of light trucks.
cues.zh: 看看在满是轻型卡车的大街上，骑车人的空间被压缩得有多小。

cues.en: And the cyclist can't see or be seen over the roof of the truck either.
cues.zh: 而且骑车人视线被车顶遮挡，既看不见别人，别人也看不见他。

cues.en: These vehicles make the streets more dangerous for everyone outside of a car and put even more pressure on already crowded city streets.
cues.zh: 这些车让所有车外人员的安全受到更大威胁，也给本就拥挤的城市道路施加了更多压力。

cues.en: Of course, SUVs don't just hit people in bike lanes or crosswalks. Their off road capability means it's easier for them to jump the curb and hit people on the sidewalk
cues.zh: 当然，SUV 不仅是在自行车道或斑马线上撞人。它们的越野能力意味着更容易冲上路牙，撞到人行道上的人，

cues.en: where they're supposed to be safe.
cues.zh: 而那里本应是最安全的地方。

cues.en: It's very likely that more SUVs on the road is a significant factor in the recent increase in pedestrian deaths in The USA, a trend that's not being seen in countries with sane vehicle sizes.
cues.zh: 路上 SUV 越来越多，极有可能是近年来美国行人死亡人数激增的重要原因，而在车辆尺寸更合理的国家根本看不到这种趋势。

cues.en: And SUVs aren't just killing the people they run into, they're also doing it through pollution.
cues.zh: 而且 SUV 不仅撞死人，还通过污染空气来害人。

cues.en: The auto industry specifically promoted SUVs to avoid CAFE emission standards.
cues.zh: 汽车行业专门推广 SUV，就是为了规避 CAFE（企业平均燃油经济性）排放标准。

cues.en: It's so bad that SUVs are the second largest factor in the rise in emissions from 2010 to 2018.
cues.zh: 问题已经严重到，SUV 成了 2010 到 2018 年间全球碳排放增长的第二大推手。

cues.en: And if SUVs were a country, they would rank seventh in the world for carbon emissions, which is more than The Netherlands and UK combined.
cues.zh: 如果把全球的 SUV 算作一个国家，其碳排放能排到全球第七，比荷兰和英国加起来还要多。

cues.en: Okay. I really don't wanna think about The Netherlands and The UK combined.
cues.zh: 好吧，我实在很难想象荷兰和英国合体是什么样。

cues.en: SUV apologists like to point out that modern SUVs are more fuel efficient than early models.
cues.zh: 为 SUV 辩护的人总喜欢强调，现在的 SUV 比早期车型更省油。

cues.en: But that comes from overall improvements in technology,
cues.zh: 但这完全归功于整体技术的进步，

cues.en: thanks to advancements in materials and manufacturing.
cues.zh: 得益于材料和制造工艺的发展。

cues.en: But a big heavy SUV is always going to use more fuel and have higher emissions than the same technology
cues.zh: 但同样的技术，用在笨重的 SUV 上，其油耗和排放

cues.en: applied to a lighter car.
cues.zh: 永远都会高于更轻便的小车。

cues.en: This is just basic physics. It takes more work to move something heavier.
cues.zh: 这只是最基础的物理规律：移动更重的物体需要做更多的功。

cues.en: This is going to cause a huge problem with the necessary transition to electric vehicles too.
cues.zh: 在向电动车转型的必然趋势下，这同样会引发巨大的问题。

cues.en: Because the heavier the vehicle, the more batteries are required to move it, and the bigger and heavier those batteries need to be.
cues.zh: 因为车越重，驱动它所需的电池就越多，电池本身也就会变得更大、更重。

cues.en: For the electric Hummer, the batteries alone weigh more than an entire typical European car.
cues.zh: 就拿电动 Hummer 来说，光是电池的重量就超过了一辆普通的欧洲小汽车。

cues.en: A few years ago, I made a video about the adoption of electric micro cars here in The Netherlands.
cues.zh: 几年前，我做过一期关于微型电动车在荷兰普及的视频。

cues.en: And I often see light electric trucks like these on the streets as well.
cues.zh: 我也经常在街上看到像这样的轻型电动卡车。

cues.en: But the gut reaction from many North Americans is to call these death machines.
cues.zh: 但许多北美人的第一直觉反应，却是把这些车称为“移动棺材”。

cues.en: But why?
cues.zh: 但这是为什么呢？

cues.en: It's because North Americans have been conditioned to believe that you need a large heavy vehicle in order to be safe on the roads.
cues.zh: 因为北美人已经被深度洗脑，认为必须开又大又重的车在路上才安全。

cues.en: We should be moving to lighter electric vehicles that require smaller batteries with better range, lower cost, and fewer resources needed to make them. But we're going in exactly
cues.zh: 我们本该转向更轻量的电动车，以更小的电池实现更长的续航、更低的成本，制造时消耗的资源也更少。但现实中，我们却完全在

cues.en: the opposite direction.
cues.zh: 背道而驰。

cues.en: Where even the smallest Tesla has a curb weight of over 1,600 kilograms
cues.zh: 就连最小的 Tesla，整备质量都超过 1600 公斤，

cues.en: significantly more than a similarly sized Toyota Yaris sedan.
cues.zh: 远重于尺寸相近的 Toyota Yaris 轿车。

cues.en: And okay. I gotta say, what the hell is up with the sport in sport utility vehicle? Are we really that stupid? There is absolutely nothing sporty about any of this.
cues.zh: 行吧，我不得不吐槽，“运动型多用途汽车”（SUV）里的“运动”到底是几个意思？我们真有那么好骗吗？这玩意儿哪有一点“运动”的样子？

cues.en: Oh, yeah.
cues.zh: 噢，对。

cues.en: Feel the burn.
cues.zh: 感受脂肪燃烧吧。

cues.en: So at this point in the video, I've likely pissed off every truck owner and they're furiously writing long angry comments about how they absolutely require an SUV for whatever reason.
cues.zh: 视频看到这儿，我大概已经惹毛了所有的皮卡车主，他们正怒气冲冲地狂敲键盘，长篇大论解释自己出于各种原因多么需要一辆 SUV。

cues.en: So let's say you live somewhere car dependent. You have 2.3 kids, routinely need to stop by Home Depot, and you wanna head out into the wilderness more than once a decade.
cues.zh: 假设你住在一个重度依赖汽车的地方，有两三个孩子，经常要逛 Home Depot，而且每隔十年至少想去野外撒把欢。

cues.en: Well, I've got good news because I've got the perfect vehicle for you.
cues.zh: 那我有个好消息，我这儿有款最适合你的车。

cues.en: A station wagon. The thing that literally every family used before auto manufacturers convinced people to buy the light trucks that made them more money. That's an estate car for all you Brits out there.
cues.zh: 旅行车（Station wagon）。在汽车厂商忽悠大家去买更赚钱的轻型卡车之前，几乎每个家庭都在开它。英国朋友们听好了，就是你们说的 estate car。

cues.en: Station wagons are more useful than SUVs for almost everyone in a city. They're easier to get in and out of, they're more maneuverable,
cues.zh: 对于绝大多数城里人来说，旅行车都比 SUV 更实用。上下车更容易，操控更灵活，

cues.en: and much easier to park in cities where, again, almost all SUV driving takes place.
cues.zh: 而且在城里也更好停车——别忘了，几乎所有的 SUV 都只是在城里开开而已。

cues.en: SUVs are built to be cool and curvy so that aging gen x'ers can pretend they never became parents, but this means that the actual usable space inside is shockingly low.
cues.zh: SUV 设计得又酷又有曲线感，好让上了年纪的 X 世代假装自己还没当爹当妈，但这也意味着其内部的实际可用空间少得惊人。

cues.en: The monstrously large Cadillac Escalade has 25.5
cues.zh: 庞然大物般的 Cadillac Escalade，最后一排座椅后面

cues.en: cubic feet of carrying space behind the last row of seats, which is less than something like a Subaru Outback or Audi a six Allroad,
cues.zh: 只有 25.5 立方英尺的储物空间，比 Subaru Outback 或 Audi A6 Allroad 这类车还要小，

cues.en: both of which have over 30. But the numbers are deceiving because the fancy design means the usable space in an Escalade is surprisingly small.
cues.zh: 后两者的空间都超过了 30 立方英尺。但单纯看数据还是保守了，因为花哨的设计导致 Escalade 的实际可用空间小得出奇。

cues.en: Of course, you can take out the rear seats of an Escalade, but you can fold down the seats of a station wagon too.
cues.zh: 当然，你可以把 Escalade 的后排座椅拆下来，但旅行车的座椅同样可以放倒啊。

cues.en: SUVs hold much less than you'd think because so much space is wasted by fancy styling, unnecessarily high ground clearance, car smashing bumpers, and pedestrian killing hoods.
cues.zh: SUV 的装载能力远不如你想象的那么大，因为大量空间都被花哨的造型、毫无必要的高离地间隙、容易撞烂前车的保险杠，以及对行人极具杀伤力的发动机舱盖给浪费掉了。

cues.en: And of course, I'm not saying that you can't carry stuff in an Escalade, only that you don't need an Escalade to carry stuff.
cues.zh: 当然，我不是说 Escalade 不能装东西，我只是说你根本不需要一辆 Escalade 来装东西。

cues.en: Have you ever tried to move a bunch of stuff with a station wagon? I have many times. It's a wide open rectangular
cues.zh: 你试过用旅行车拉一大堆东西吗？我拉过很多次。它就是一个敞敞亮亮的

cues.en: cuboid of spacious goodness.
cues.zh: 长方体大空间，简直绝了。

cues.en: A station wagon is a superior vehicle for families. More storage space, better fuel efficiency, and plenty of room for kids,
cues.zh: 旅行车绝对是更优秀的家用车型。储物空间更大，油耗更低，给孩子的空间也绰绰有余，

cues.en: which is why they're still very common in Europe.
cues.zh: 这也是为什么它们在欧洲依然随处可见。

cues.en: The reason you don't see station wagons in The US anymore is because automakers could make more money convincing Jennifer, Mike, Dave, Amy, and Kimberly that station wagons were uncool because apparently
cues.zh: 而在美国看不到旅行车，纯粹是因为车企为了多赚钱，忽悠普通消费者觉得开旅行车很丢人，因为在他们眼里，

cues.en: this is cool.
cues.zh: 这种才叫“酷”。

cues.en: And if you really need a lot of space or seating a regular basis, a minivan beats an SUV
cues.zh: 如果你真的经常需要很大空间或很多座位，minivan 就是比 SUV 强

cues.en: every time. I've seen this myself when we once booked a large taxi to the airport and they sent us Suburban.
cues.zh: 每次都是。我自己就见过：有次我们订了去机场的大出租车，结果他们派来一辆 Suburban。

cues.en: Our luggage wouldn't even fit in the back and we had to put some of it on our laps.
cues.zh: 我们的行李连后备厢都放不下，只好把一些搁在腿上。

cues.en: But when we got to our destination,
cues.zh: 但到了目的地时，

cues.en: our taxi was a minivan and everything fit comfortably in the back.
cues.zh: 我们的出租车是一辆 minivan，所有东西都舒舒服服地放进后备厢。

cues.en: A minivan will hold more stuff and it's easier for passengers to get in and out of too because the doors are bigger and it's lower to the ground.
cues.zh: minivan 能装更多东西，乘客上下车也更方便，因为车门更大，车身也更低。

cues.en: But after a few decades, Americans are getting bored of SUVs. So automakers are trying to promote pickup trucks as the new family vehicle, which is even more ridiculous.
cues.zh: 但几十年后，美国人开始对 SUV 感到厌倦。于是车企试图把皮卡宣传成新的家庭用车，这就更荒唐了。

cues.en: At least SUVs had a cover over your cargo.
cues.zh: 至少 SUV 还能把你的货物盖起来。

cues.en: Of course, Ford knows this is ridiculous too.
cues.zh: 当然，Ford 也知道这很荒唐。

cues.en: While they were promoting the f one fifty pickup to Americans as the perfect family vehicle,
cues.zh: 他们在向美国人把 F-150 皮卡宣传成完美家庭用车的同时，

cues.en: they used the exact same marketing language to market the seven seat s max to Europeans because
cues.zh: 却用一模一样的营销话术，向欧洲人推销七座 S-Max，因为

cues.en: European regulations make it harder to profit from upselling people to light trucks.
cues.zh: 欧洲法规让人更难通过引导消费者升级到轻型卡车来赚钱。

cues.en: Let's be really clear here. American automakers are not promoting SUVs and pickup trucks because they're practical.
cues.zh: 这里要说清楚。美国车企推销 SUV 和皮卡，并不是因为它们实用。

cues.en: They do it because it makes them more money.
cues.zh: 他们这么做是因为这样更赚钱。

cues.en: It's very apparent in Europe that actual tradespeople,
cues.zh: 在欧洲很明显，真正的行业从业者，

cues.en: you know, the people who actually need a vehicle with lots of space on a regular basis, almost universally
cues.zh: 你知道，就是那些经常确实需要大空间车辆的人，几乎无一例外

cues.en: choose vans.
cues.zh: 会选择厢式车。

cues.en: A typical European van will easily carry more than a pickup truck and certainly more than an SUV, and the lower bed is easier to load too.
cues.zh: 一辆典型的欧洲厢式车，装东西轻松超过皮卡，当然更超过 SUV，而且货台更低，装货也更容易。

cues.en: I really struggle to understand how a DHL delivery driver can do his job with a Kangoo van,
cues.zh: 我真的很难理解，一个 DHL 快递司机怎么能靠 Kangoo 厢式车完成工作，

cues.en: But a middle aged suburbanite thinks they need a Chevy Silverado to buy groceries.
cues.zh: 而一个中年郊区居民却觉得自己需要一辆 Chevy Silverado 去买菜。

cues.en: And to be fair, these vans can get quite big, but that space is used to make it efficiently carry lots of stuff. And they still have a design that is safer in a crash and gives the driver good visibility,
cues.zh: 平心而论，这些厢式车可以做得很大，但那些空间是用来高效装大量东西的。而且它们的设计在碰撞中更安全，也给司机良好视野，

cues.en: proving that it is possible to provide all the goods and services a city needs without needlessly murdering people.
cues.zh: 这证明，城市所需的所有商品和服务，是可以在不必无谓撞死人的情况下提供的。

cues.en: One of these vehicles is designed to efficiently carry lots of useful stuff, while the other is designed to carry fragile egos.
cues.zh: 这些车中，有一类是设计来高效装载大量有用物品的，另一类则是设计来承载脆弱自尊的。

cues.en: And I'm not even gonna go into the fact that so many professionals here in The Netherlands, whether they're a handyman or doing package delivery,
cues.zh: 我甚至都不想说，在荷兰有那么多专业人士，不管是做维修工还是送快递，

cues.en: can do their job just fine using cargo bikes.
cues.zh: 都能靠货运自行车把活干得好好的。

cues.en: A pickup truck is mostly useful if you're loading heavy dirty items into the bed, like on a farm
cues.zh: 皮卡主要是在你要把又重又脏的东西装进车斗时才有用，比如在农场

cues.en: construction sites. So outside of The US, that's usually the only place you'll find them.
cues.zh: 或建筑工地。所以在美国以外，通常只有这些地方才见得到皮卡。

cues.en: For almost any other use case for moving people or cargo, a van or minivan is a better option.
cues.zh: 对于几乎任何其他载人或运货的场景，厢式货车或小型客货车都是更好的选择。

cues.en: And the thing that frustrates me the most about all this is that when city advocates complain about the insane growth in oversized trucks in our cities,
cues.zh: 而整件事最让我抓狂的是，当城市拥护者抱怨城市里超大皮卡疯狂增长时，

cues.en: a bunch of people come out of the woodwork claiming that those drivers really need that cargo space.
cues.zh: 总会冒出一帮人辩称，那些司机真的需要那么大的装载空间。

cues.en: But consider that the Ford f one fifty was the single most popular vehicle sold in America
cues.zh: 但想想看，Ford F-150 是全美销量最高的单一车型，

cues.en: Literally
cues.zh: 货真价实的

cues.en: number one.
cues.zh: 第一名。

cues.en: Yet forty years ago in 1982,
cues.zh: 然而 40 年前的 1982 年，

cues.en: the number one vehicle was the Ford Escort.
cues.zh: 销量第一的车型还是 Ford Escort。

cues.en: Are you seriously telling me the cargo hauling behavior of Americans has changed that much in forty years?
cues.zh: 你真觉得美国人的货运习惯在 40 年里发生了这么大的变化吗？

cues.en: Are you really proposing that all of these empty pickup trucks you see all over The US and Canada with pristine shiny tailgates are just extremely
cues.zh: 你真认为在美加各地看到的那些后斗空空、尾门锃光瓦亮的皮卡，都只是

cues.en: careful construction workers that just happen to be between loads?
cues.zh: 碰巧处于空载间隙、格外爱惜车的建筑工人吗？

cues.en: Or is it the much more likely explanation that these people have been upsold on these vehicles by automakers looking to skirt regulations to make higher profits?
cues.zh: 还是说更合理的解释是：车企为了规避监管赚取更高利润，向这些人兜售了更昂贵的车型？

cues.en: In fact, these pickup trucks have become heavier and less practical over the past forty years.
cues.zh: 事实上，过去 40 年里，这些皮卡变得越来越重，实用性却越来越差。

cues.en: This Axios article is a great read, link in the description, but the best part is this graphic showing how the size of the truck bed has changed over the years. These are clearly morphing from practical farm vehicles into status symbols for insecure suburbanites with a cargo fetish.
cues.zh: Axios 的这篇文章非常值得一读，链接在简介里，但最精彩的是这张图表，展示了货斗尺寸多年来的演变——它们显然正从实用的农用车辆，变成缺乏安全感、有载货癖好的郊区中产的身份象征。

cues.en: And to be perfectly blunt, it's pretty insulting to our intelligence to suggest that all these new pick up trucks are really needed for hauling.
cues.zh: 坦白讲，要是硬说买这些新皮卡全是为了拉货，简直是在侮辱我们的智商。

cues.en: But as extended cab pickups become the new suburban assault vehicles to wine moms everywhere,
cues.zh: 但随着加长双排皮卡成为各地郊区妈妈们的新型“装甲突击车”，

cues.en: there's been a surge in interest in older pickup models as actual contractors seek vehicles that are more practical.
cues.zh: 真正干活的承包商却开始抢购老款皮卡，试图寻找更实用的车型。

cues.en: They're easier to load because they're lower to the ground, easier to maneuver and park at job sites, and the size of the bed is usually larger too.
cues.zh: 老款底盘更低更易装货，在工地上更好操控和停靠，而且货斗尺寸通常也更大。

cues.en: You can still order a new pickup with a longer bed, but they're a special order that can take months to arrive. Well, you can drive an extended cab pickup off the lot today.
cues.zh: 你虽然仍能订购长斗的新皮卡，但属于特殊订制，得等上好几个月；而加长双排皮卡，你今天去展厅就能直接提车开走。

cues.en: The only guy who shows up on the job site in the shiny new f one fifty Raptor Super Crew
cues.zh: 唯一开着崭新的 Ford F-150 Raptor SuperCrew 现身工地的，

cues.en: is the owner's son who's cosplaying as a blue collar laborer.
cues.zh: 只有大老板家来体验蓝领生活的公子哥。

cues.en: So SUVs and light trucks are oversized impractical vehicles which were heavily marketed to impressionable people because they make more money for automakers by skirting regulations.
cues.zh: 所以，SUV 和轻型皮卡就是体型庞大且不实用的车，车企通过钻监管空子赚取暴利，再将它们大肆推销给容易跟风的人。

cues.en: And while the average SUV buyer in the early two thousands was likely a sociopath and or easily manipulated by marketing, nowadays,
cues.zh: 如果说在 2000 年代初，买 SUV 的普通人多半是缺乏社会公德，或是容易被营销洗脑，那么到了今天，

cues.en: it's not so clear.
cues.zh: 情况就没那么简单了。

cues.en: American automakers have literally turned off the production of station wagons, sedans, and smaller vehicles to focus almost exclusively on the more lucrative market for light trucks.
cues.zh: 美国汽车制造商真的已经停产旅行车、轿车和更小型车辆，几乎完全转向利润更高的轻卡市场。

cues.en: People argue that consumers prefer SUVs and automakers are just responding to demand, but that demand is coming off the back of billions of dollars in advertising and marketing pushed because SUVs are artificially cheaper than they should be thanks to the light truck exemption.
cues.zh: 有人说消费者偏爱 SUV，汽车制造商只是在回应需求，但这种需求背后是数十亿美元的广告和营销推动，因为轻卡豁免让 SUV 被人为压低到低于应有价格。

cues.en: And as the road safety arm race makes vehicles bigger, people are rationally concerned about their safety and gravitate toward larger vehicles to protect themselves.
cues.zh: 随着道路安全军备竞赛让车辆越做越大，人们有充分理由担心自身安全，并倾向于选择更大的车来保护自己。

cues.en: So a new class of vehicle has emerged, the crossover,
cues.zh: 于是出现了一类新车型——跨界车，

cues.en: which is an SUV built on a car frame instead of a truck frame.
cues.zh: 它是在轿车车架而非卡车车架上打造的 SUV。

cues.en: But fundamentally,
cues.zh: 但说到底，

cues.en: these are just cars that are bigger than they need to be. Cars with more ground clearance than is necessary. Cars with a higher bumper than is safe. Cars with lower fuel economy than if they were lighter.
cues.zh: 这些车本质上只是比实际需要更大的轿车：离地间隙高过必要程度，保险杠高到不安全，燃油经济性也比更轻时更差。

cues.en: But they're popular because people are rightfully scared about sharing the road with giant SUVs and pickup trucks. So
cues.zh: 但它们很受欢迎，因为人们有理由害怕与巨型 SUV 和皮卡共享道路。所以

cues.en: I can't really blame Americans for wanting to buy SUVs and crossovers today.
cues.zh: 如今美国人想买 SUV 和跨界车，我真不能怪他们。

cues.en: I would probably do the same thing if I were forced to live somewhere like this.
cues.zh: 如果我被迫住在这样的地方，我大概也会这么做。

cues.en: Of course, the most vulnerable people are those who can't participate in the arms race. Everyone who's not in a car.
cues.zh: 当然，最脆弱的是无法参与这场军备竞赛的人——所有不在车里的人。

cues.en: So what are we gonna do about it?
cues.zh: 那我们该怎么办？

cues.en: The first solution is to close the light truck loophole that allows these ridiculous vehicles on the road in the first place.
cues.zh: 第一个解决方案是堵上轻卡漏洞，正是它让这些荒唐车辆得以一开始就上路。

cues.en: Light trucks should be required to meet all the same safety standards as every other passenger vehicle, and they need to be safer in crashes, lighter, and have much better fuel economy.
cues.zh: 应要求轻卡满足与其他所有乘用车完全相同的安全标准，并在碰撞中更安全、更轻、燃油经济性大幅提升。

cues.en: Unfortunately,
cues.zh: 不幸的是，

cues.en: the recent changes to the CAFE standards in 2021
cues.zh: 2021 年对 CAFE 标准的最新修改

cues.en: still have the light truck exemption in place.
cues.zh: 仍然保留了轻卡豁免。

cues.en: And even some crossovers like the Honda CR V and Toyota RAV four can be put in the light truck category depending on how they're configured.
cues.zh: 甚至一些跨界车，比如 Honda CR-V 和 Toyota RAV4，根据配置方式也能被归入轻卡类别。

cues.en: The US could also remove the import restrictions and duties on light trucks that are still around today.
cues.zh: 美国也可以取消今天仍然存在的轻卡进口限制和关税。

cues.en: They're the reason why you won't see smaller, more practical, foreign built trucks like these in American cities.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么你在美国城市里看不到像这些更小、更实用、海外制造的卡车。

cues.en: And you won't see these small electric trucks coming to market there either.
cues.zh: 这些小型电动卡车也不会在那里上市。

cues.en: What's also desperately needed for all vehicles is for pedestrian tests and crash compatibility
cues.zh: 所有车辆还迫切需要的是，让行人测试和碰撞兼容性

cues.en: to have a more prominent role in determining safety ratings.
cues.zh: 在确定安全评级时发挥更重要的作用。

cues.en: And now that light trucks are mainstream vehicles, they should be tested for safety and fuel efficiency the exact same way that other vehicles are.
cues.zh: 既然轻卡已是主流车辆，它们就应该和其他车辆完全一样接受安全性和燃油经济性测试。

cues.en: For example, in The US, the frontal crash tests done by the NHTSA
cues.zh: 例如，在美国，NHTSA 进行的正面碰撞测试

cues.en: are only done with vehicles in the same weight class.
cues.zh: 只在同等重量级别的车辆之间进行。

cues.en: Why do we accept this? It's not like SUVs have their own class of roads.
cues.zh: 我们凭什么接受这种设定？SUV 又没有自己的专属道路。

cues.en: All vehicles share the same roads, so they should all be crash compatible with one another.
cues.zh: 所有车辆都在同一条路上跑，碰撞相容性本就应该彼此兼顾。

cues.en: I'd like to see different classes of vehicles tested against each other and to dock points if a vehicle causes significant damage to vehicles of another class.
cues.zh: 我更希望看到不同级别的车辆进行相互对撞测试，如果某种车对其他级别的车造成严重破坏，就该扣分。

cues.en: Cities in particular should be doing a lot more to regulate SUVs.
cues.zh: 尤其是各大城市，应该采取更多措施来监管 SUV。

cues.en: They go against every goal that cities have. To reduce the effects of climate change, to reduce pedestrian deaths, to reduce traffic, to maintain roads, and to make best use of the limited space available.
cues.zh: 它们与城市的所有目标都背道而驰：减缓气候变化、减少行人伤亡、缓解交通拥堵、养护道路，以及充分利用有限的空间。

cues.en: Cities should tax vehicles by weight and limit vehicles with bumpers that are too high or require commercial driver's licenses to operate them. Parking permits for longer vehicles should be more expensive to compensate for the lost space.
cues.zh: 城市应该按车重征税，限制保险杠过高的车辆，或者要求持有商用驾照才能驾驶。车身更长的车辆，停车许可证应该更贵，以弥补占用的空间。

cues.en: Licensing and insuring SUVs should be more expensive too.
cues.zh: SUV 的上牌和车险费用也理应更高。

cues.en: And since a big part of road safety is the kinetic energy of the crash, which comes from mass and velocity,
cues.zh: 而且道路安全很大程度上取决于碰撞时的动能，而动能来自质量与速度，

cues.en: then if the weight keeps increasing, we should be decreasing the speed. In other words, cities can and should be lowering speed limits in response to heavier vehicles.
cues.zh: 那么如果车重持续增加，我们就应该降低车速。换句话说，面对越来越重的车辆，城市完全可以也应该降低限速。

cues.en: These are all great ideas, but right now cities are doing basically nothing to stop the spread of SUVs and pickup trucks.
cues.zh: 这些想法都很好，但目前各大城市在遏制 SUV 和皮卡泛滥方面基本毫无作为。

cues.en: Here in The Netherlands, cars are taxed more depending on their weight, but the increase is minimal.
cues.zh: 在我们荷兰，汽车税确实会随车重递增，但涨幅微乎其微。

cues.en: And North American cities are doing even less. Washington DC will introduce a higher vehicle registration fee for heavier vehicles, but this only applies to the absolute highest weight class of over 6,000
cues.zh: 而北美城市做得更少。华盛顿特区虽然准备对较重的车辆加收注册费，但这仅适用于最高重量级别——超过 6000

cues.en: pounds.
cues.zh: 磅的车辆。

cues.en: So with effectively nothing being done to slow the adoption of heavier vehicles, some people are taking matters into their own hands.
cues.zh: 既然没有有效措施来遏制重型车辆的普及，有些人便开始自己动手了。

cues.en: A group calling themselves the tire extinguishers have started deflating the tires of SUVs in Europe. It's unclear whether this is a crime.
cues.zh: 一个自称“轮胎灭绝者”的群体，已经开始在欧洲给 SUV 的轮胎放气。这是否构成犯罪尚无定论。

cues.en: Their stated goal is to make it impossible to own an SUV in the city.
cues.zh: 他们宣称的目标，就是让人们彻底无法在城市里拥有 SUV。

cues.en: Now obviously this is really extreme behavior, but but let's be clear. This group only exists because of the complete and utter regulatory silence that has come from city and federal governments when it comes to curbing the problems caused by SUVs in cities.
cues.zh: 这显然是非常极端的行为，但我们必须讲清楚：这个群体的出现，完全是因为在应对城市中 SUV 造成的种种问题时，市政和联邦政府彻底处于监管失语状态。

cues.en: And even if The US is too far gone, European cities need to deal with this issue immediately.
cues.zh: 哪怕美国已经积重难返，欧洲城市也必须立刻着手解决这个问题。

cues.en: SUVs and crossovers now account for 40% of all vehicles sold in The EU, a 900%
cues.zh: 目前 SUV 和跨界车已占欧盟汽车总销量的 40%，增幅高达 900%

cues.en: increase since 2001.
I don't think Europeans realize how bad this can get.
cues.zh: 我觉得欧洲人还没意识到情况能有多糟。

cues.en: I hear people justifiably
cues.zh: 我听到人们有充分理由地

cues.en: complaining about the infestation of giant Land Rovers in European cities.
cues.zh: 抱怨欧洲城市里巨型 Land Rover 泛滥成灾。

cues.en: But look at how small this Range Rover looks next to a full sized American SUV.
cues.zh: 但看看这辆 Range Rover 在全尺寸美国 SUV 旁边显得多小。

cues.en: Europe needs to get ahead of SUVs and pickup trucks now before more Europeans end up under them.
cues.zh: 欧洲现在就得抢先应对 SUV 和皮卡，别等更多欧洲人被它们压在轮下。

cues.en: Fundamentally,
cues.zh: 从根本上说，

cues.en: SUVs are a plague on cities. They're impractical, dangerous, expensive, and polluting, but car manufacturers have spent billions of dollars to convince you to think otherwise.
cues.zh: SUV 是城市的瘟疫。它们不实用、危险、昂贵又污染环境，但汽车制造商花了几十亿美元让你相信并非如此。

cues.en: Don't fall for it. Let your local representatives know you're not okay with these suburban assault vehicles taking over our roads.
cues.zh: 别上当。告诉你所在地区的代表，你不接受这些郊区突击车霸占我们的道路。

cues.en: Ultimately,
cues.zh: 说到底，

cues.en: this really is about freedom.
cues.zh: 这真的关乎自由。

cues.en: The freedom to get around however we want. The freedom to drive a small and efficient car without worrying about the road safety arms race. Or even better, the freedom to not to have to drive, to get around by walking, cycling, and public transit without the constant threat of serious injury or death from bloated, oversized trucks.
cues.zh: 想怎么出行就怎么出行的自由。开一辆小巧高效汽车的自由，不必担心道路安全军备竞赛。或者更好，是不必开车的自由——步行、骑车、坐公交出行，而无需时刻面临被臃肿超大卡车严重伤害或致死的威胁。

cues.en: And finally,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: since the typical light truck driver is so status obsessed, let's use that to our advantage.
cues.zh: 既然典型的轻型卡车司机那么痴迷身份地位，那就让我们利用这一点。

cues.en: So when you see someone driving a truck like this, let them know they look like a fucking idiot.
cues.zh: 所以看到有人开这种卡车，就告诉他们：你看起来就是个他妈的蠢货。

cues.en: Get a station wagon, loser.
cues.zh: 买辆旅行车吧，废物。

cues.en: If you've made it this far into the video without rage quitting, then you might just be ready to learn more about good urbanism.
cues.zh: 如果你看到这里还没气得退出视频，那你可能正好准备好了解什么是优秀城市主义。

cues.en: It's not about hating cars. It's about building wonderful cities that are designed for people.
cues.zh: 这不是要讨厌汽车，而是要建设为人而设计的精彩城市。

cues.en: Though admittedly,
cues.zh: 虽然得承认，

cues.en: the smaller the cars, the better.
cues.zh: 车越小越好。

cues.en: But you don't just have to take my word for it. Online urbanism has become a movement, and we're spoiled for choice when it comes to great creators these days.
cues.zh: 但你不必只听我说。线上城市主义已经成为一场运动，如今优秀创作者多到让我们挑不过来。

cues.en: And did you know that many of these urbanist creators are on Nebula?
cues.zh: 你知道吗，这些城市主义创作者中有很多都在 Nebula 上？

cues.en: The most recent addition is City Nerd who makes weekly video essays about cities in The US and abroad.
cues.zh: 最新加入的是 City Nerd，他每周做视频随笔，聊美国和国外的城市。
